value.answer: This sounds like it could be hand-foot-and-mouth disease, common in preschoolers - a mild viral illness causing mouth sores, a low fever, and often a rash on hands/feet. It usually clears in 7-10 days with rest and fluids. Watch for refusing all liquids, fewer wet diapers/pee, or getting more sluggish - mouth pain can make kids stop drinking.
value.triage: Call Health811 (811) if fever lasts more than a couple days, mouth pain is stopping fluids, or you're unsure. Go to the ER or call 911 if there are signs of dehydration (no urine 8+ hours, very dry mouth, lethargic), trouble breathing, a stiff neck, or a fever with a rash that does not fade when pressed.
value.sources: CDC - Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease","HealthyChildren.org (AAP)","Caring for Kids (CPS)
